# F02 - Image hierarchy: group layout, arbitrary level names, dimension ordering (witness: verified)

**Independent finding identity.** Each OME-Zarr image is a Zarr group whose group-level attributes live in zarr.json and include multiscales and (optionally) omero. Each multiscale resolution level is a separate Zarr array; array names are arbitrary with ordering defined by the multiscales metadata, though often a sequence starting at 0. Image arrays must be up to 5-dimensional with the time axis before channel before spatial axes. Dimension count is variable between 2 and 5 and axis names are arbitrary. An optional labels group sits at the same level as the resolution arrays and holds a list of label images; label dimensions must equal the corresponding image dimension or be 1 if irrelevant; intermediate folders are permitted and contain no extra metadata; label multiscale arrays support only integer values.

**Governing conditions.** Level ordering comes from metadata, not names: a reader sorting directories lexically or numerically without consulting multiscales.datasets can present pyramids in the wrong order. Time-before-channel-before-space axis order is an obligation on data, reliable only after confirming the axes metadata (see F05, F08).

**Verification evidence.** S003 sha256 5d8b240877ed2cf9596566187bcb3779ea011d5319807134c65e2e7dc2ae82de: lines 87-89 (group with multiscales and omero attributes), 91-94 (separate arrays, arbitrary names, ordering from multiscales metadata), 96-97 (up to 5-D, time before channel before space), 81 (2-5 dimensions, arbitrary axis names), 102-108 (labels group, listing, dimension equality or 1), 110 (intermediate folders, no extra metadata), 116-117 (integer values only); corroborated by line 426 (omero optional). Plan mapping: S002:Slice 02 sha256 569f317fd651ce08911196d023cefd1f8919d1dcebe244c79397337f8c279006. Negative search over S003 lines 1-896 found no competing ordering rule; no statement permits inferring level order from array names.

**Plan implications.** Slice 02 fileset opening and listing must be metadata-driven: discover images by groups with multiscales, resolve pyramid levels via datasets[].path order, never infer semantics from folder names. The labels container is the discovery route for overlays (F10).

# F03 - High-content screening (HCS) hierarchy: plate, row, well, field of view (witness: verified)

**Independent finding identity.** For HCS datasets, three groups MUST be defined above the images: the group above the images is a well and MUST implement the well specification; the group above the well is a row; the group above the row is a plate that MUST implement the plate specification. A well row group SHOULD NOT be present if there are no images in that row, and a well group SHOULD NOT be present if there are no images in the well. All images in a well are fields of view of the same well. The example hierarchy shows plate zarr.json, row directories, column directories implementing well, and per-field groups implementing multiscales and omero with their own resolution levels and optional labels.

**Governing conditions.** MUST-level: well and plate groups implement their specifications (detail in F11, F12). SHOULD-level: empty rows/wells SHOULD NOT exist, so a conforming fileset may legitimately be sparse; the viewer cannot assume a full rectangular grid.

**Verification evidence.** S003 sha256 5d8b240877ed2cf9596566187bcb3779ea011d5319807134c65e2e7dc2ae82de: lines 119-127 (three groups MUST; well and plate implement their specifications), 121-123 (all images in a well are fields of view), 128-129 (empty rows/wells SHOULD NOT be present), 132-148 (worked hierarchy example). Plan mapping: S002:Slice 02 sha256 569f317fd651ce08911196d023cefd1f8919d1dcebe244c79397337f8c279006. Negative search over S003 lines 1-896 found no statement permitting directory scanning as the discovery route for fields, and no requirement that plates be dense.

**Plan implications.** Image discovery inside an HCS fileset must traverse plate, rows, wells, fields, enumerating fields via well.images, not by scanning directories. Sparse plates are expected, not exceptional. Field groups are ordinary multiscale images reusing the normal image pipeline. The thin plan's generic image listing needs a plate-aware presentation (with F11/F12) to satisfy the brief's find-images requirement.

**Semantic ambiguity: no.** Claims are fully determined by admitted source; whether extra intermediate groups under a well are permitted is a documented silence, not ambiguous text.

**Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED):** sparse-plate and multi-field fixtures (mirroring S003 lines 641-739) exercised through the discovery path; assert fields come only from well.images.

# F05 - Axes metadata: names, types, units, dimension_names (witness: verified)

**Independent finding identity.** axes is a list of dictionaries describing the dimensions of a physical coordinate space. Each dictionary MUST contain name, with values unique across all name fields; SHOULD contain type, one of space, time, channel, but MAY take other custom string values; SHOULD contain unit, whose value SHOULD be a UDUNITS-2 valid string. Explicit allowed unit vocabularies are enumerated for space axes (angstrom through zettameter) and time axes (attosecond through zettasecond). The length of axes MUST equal the number of dimensions of the arrays holding the image data. The dimension_names attribute MUST be included in the zarr.json of the Zarr array of each multiscale level and MUST match the names in the axes metadata.

**Governing conditions.** MUST: unique names; axes length equals array dimensionality; dimension_names present in array metadata and matching axes. SHOULD (not guaranteed): type and unit present and standard - a conforming file can omit units or use custom axis types.

# F06 - bioformats2raw.layout transitional collections and reader obligations for multi-image filesets (witness: verified)

**Independent finding identity.** Transitional bioformats2raw.layout metadata identifies a group that implicitly describes a series of images, added in v0.4 to specify filesets that already exist in the wild; an upcoming NGFF specification will replace it. Layout: top-level zarr.json with the layout key, an OME group holding series metadata and METADATA.ome.xml, and consecutively numbered image groups 0, 1, ... Conforming groups MUST have value 3 for the bioformats2raw.layout key at the top of the hierarchy and SHOULD have OME-XML in OME/METADATA.ome.xml adhering to the OME-XML specification with <MetadataOnly/> rather than <BinData/>, <BinaryOnly/> or <TiffData/>. If the top-level group is a plate, the plate key MUST also be present, takes precedence, and parsing should follow the plate specification; mixing image collections with plates is not possible. Image-location logic: with plate metadata, images MUST be at the defined locations; series SHOULD be provided for tools unaware of plates; if the OME group has series, it MUST be a list of strings, each a path to an image group, whose order MUST match the order of Image elements in the OME-XML if provided; if no series and no plate, separate multiscales images MUST be stored in consecutively numbered groups starting from 0, each representing exactly one OME-XML Image in the same order. Reader obligations: readers SHOULD make users aware of more than one image (SHOULD NOT default to only opening the first); MAY use series; MAY show all images or offer a choice; MAY ignore other groups or arrays under the root.

**Governing conditions.** MUST: layout value 3; series as string list; order constraints; numbered-groups fallback. SHOULD: surface multiple images rather than silently opening the first; OME-XML details. MAY: presentation choice and ignoring unrelated groups.

**Verification evidence.** S003 sha256 5d8b240877ed2cf9596566187bcb3779ea011d5319807134c65e2e7dc2ae82de: lines 175-181 (transitional status, v0.4 origin, future replacement), 182-191 (layout), 204-206 (plate precedence, no mixing), 243-253 (series example), 255-260 (MUST value 3; OME-XML SHOULD/MUST/MAY), 261-270 (location logic), 271-275 (reader obligations). # F07 - coordinateTransformations vocabulary and application order (witness: verified)

**Independent finding identity.** coordinateTransformations describe transformations mapping between coordinate spaces defined by axes, for example mapping a discrete data space of an array to the corresponding physical space. It is a list of dictionaries; each entry MUST contain type, whose value MUST be one of: identity (the default, typically not explicitly defined), translation, or scale. translation and scale each store a vector either inline as translation/scale lists of floats or as binary data at a location in this container via path; the vector length defines the number of dimensions. Transformations in the list are applied sequentially and in order.

**Governing conditions.** MUST: each entry has a valid type. The inline-versus-path alternative is part of the normative field table, so conforming files may store transforms as binary data by path. Sequential application order is normative.

**Verification evidence.** S003 sha256 5d8b240877ed2cf9596566187bcb3779ea011d5319807134c65e2e7dc2ae82de: lines 277-278 (purpose), 279-281 (list of dictionaries, MUST contain type, value from table), 282-283 (identity default), 284-286 (translation: inline list or path; vector length defines dimensions), 287-289 (scale: inline list or path; same rule), 293 (applied sequentially and in order). Plan mapping: S002:Slice 02 sha256 569f317fd651ce08911196d023cefd1f8919d1dcebe244c79397337f8c279006. Negative search over S003 lines 1-896 found no other transformation types and no defined binary layout for path-referenced vectors.

**Plan implications.** Correct calibrated coordinates (Slice 02 details panel) require composing dataset-level then group-level transforms (order fixed in F08) as sequential operations: physical = scale applied to index, plus translation, in list order. Supporting only inline arrays and silently misreading path-based transforms would produce wrong coordinates for conforming files; path-form support is a correctness requirement for full conformance, though its practical frequency is unknown (product scoping decision with a documented limitation if deferred).

**Semantic ambiguity: yes - unresolved.** The binary layout (array name, dtype, byte order) of path-referenced transform data is not specified anywhere in the admitted corpus; implementing it requires assumptions or future source work. Retained as unresolved area.

**Proposed validation (UNEXECUTED):** build a path-form transform fixture per the Zarr v3 binary convention; verify coordinate readout matches the inline equivalent before deciding to support path-form.

# F08 - multiscales metadata: pyramid obligations and calibration rules (witness: verified)

**Independent finding identity.** Image metadata lives under the multiscales key in group-level OME-Zarr metadata; an image is 2 to 5 dimensional data with optional time or channel axes, stored in multiple resolutions. Each multiscales dictionary MUST contain axes, of length 2-5 equal to array dimensionality; axes MUST contain 2 or 3 space entries and MAY add one time and one channel or null/custom-type entry; entries MUST be ordered time first, then channel/custom, then space, matching array dimension order; for three spatial axes stacked along z, order SHOULD be zyx. Each dictionary MUST contain datasets, a list describing resolution levels; each dataset MUST contain path relative to the current group, ordered from largest (highest resolution) to smallest; all datasets MUST have the same number of dimensions, not more than 5, matching axes. Each dataset MUST contain coordinateTransformations mapping data coordinates to physical coordinates for that level; transformations MUST only be of type translation or scale; they MUST contain exactly one scale transformation specifying pixel size in physical units or time duration, or, when scaling is unavailable for an axis, the factor versus the first resolution defaulting to 1.0; MAY contain exactly one translation, which MUST be listed after scale; scale and translation array lengths MUST equal the axes length. Each multiscales dictionary MAY contain group-level coordinateTransformations applied to all levels after the dataset-level ones, under the same type/order rules. SHOULD fields: name, type of downscaling method, metadata about the method; a full example with per-level scales and a group-level time scale appears at lines 320-387. When multiple multiscales entries exist, the user can choose by name with the first as fallback (pseudocode lines 388-397).

**Governing conditions.** MUST: axes; datasets; path order largest-to-smallest; exactly one scale per dataset; translation (if any) after scale; length equalities; dimension constraints. SHOULD: zyx spatial order; name/type/metadata fields. MAY: group-level transforms; translation at all.

**Verification evidence.** S003 sha256 5d8b240877ed2cf9596566187bcb3779ea011d5319807134c65e2e7dc2ae82de: lines 295-298 (location and shape), 299-303 (axes rules incl. zyx SHOULD), 304-307 (datasets, path order, dimension rules), 308-313 (coordinateTransformations MUST rules, exactly one scale, default 1.0, translation after scale, length equality), 314-316 (group-level transforms applied after dataset-level), 317-319 (SHOULD name/type/metadata), 320-387 (full example), 388-397 (selection pseudocode). Plan mapping: S002:Slice 02 sha256 569f317fd651ce08911196d023cefd1f8919d1dcebe244c79397337f8c279006. Negative search over S003 lines 1-896 found no rule allowing non-scale/translation types in multiscales and no alternative ordering guarantee.

**Plan implications.** The Slice 02 pyramid-level choice must enumerate datasets in listed order (largest first) and pick by view fit/chunk cost; level ordering and count are normative. Physical calibration is always derivable in principle because scale is mandatory (defaulting to 1.0), so the details panel can always compute data-to-physical mapping, composing dataset-level then group-level transforms in order. Multiple named multiscales require a chooser or a documented first-entry fallback. Slice 03 large-read behavior relies on chunk-aligned level reads.

**Semantic ambiguity: no.** The section is fully normative and self-contained in the corpus; handling of non-conforming cases is product work retained as unresolved area U8.

# F10 - labels and image-label: overlay discovery, dtypes, colors, alignment (witness: verified)

**Independent finding identity.** Label images are pixel-annotation arrays with integer values of custom meaning, stored in a labels group nested within the image group at the same level as the resolution arrays. # F13 - Transitional metadata policy, JSON strictness, and naming style (witness: verified)

**Independent finding identity.** Transitional metadata is added with the intention of removing it in the future; implementations may be expected (MUST) or encouraged (SHOULD) to support reading it, while writing is usually optional (MAY); examples include custom additions later formalized. Multi-word keys should use camelCase, though some parts of the specification predate this convention and are to be updated in due course.
